extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of public relations; PR educators
extracted.subtask_description: An introductory textbook overview of core public relations principles, professional standards, the four-step management process (research, planning, action, evaluation), and practice contexts. Intended to guide classroom learning and professional reference for strategic PR work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define public relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Define public relations as the management function that builds and maintains relationships between organizations and their publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book presents public relations as a management function establishing and maintaining mutually beneficial relationships between an organization and the publics on whom its success or failure depends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish public relations from marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between public relations and marketing, identifying the exchange between provider and customer as the distinguishing characteristic of marketing relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize that marketing centers on exchange between provider and customer while PR focuses on managing relationships with multiple publics; chapter aims to clarify frequently confused terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate related concepts (publicity, advertising, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe and differentiate among related concepts—publicity, advertising, press agentry, employee relations, community relations, public affairs, issues management, crisis communication, lobbying, investor relations, and development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 1 instructs students to be able to define and distinguish these adjacent functions and specialties within the communication field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain PR's contribution to organizations and society
rubrics_metrics.description: Outline how public relations helps improve organizations and society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learning outcome to articulate PR's role in organizational improvement and broader societal functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-step public relations process
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the four-step public relations process: Step One—Defining public relations problems; Step Two—Planning and programming; Step Three—Taking action and communicating; Step Four—Evaluating the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The model demonstrates logic of using research to benchmark programs, then planning, implementing (including corrective action), and evaluating (closing the loop on benchmarking). The model is used throughout Chapters 11–14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step One: Defining public relations problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Use research to detect, explore, and describe public relations situations and to 'benchmark' the beginning of the program by defining problems and setting program goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes discussion of research attitude, listening as systematic research, informal/exploratory methods, formal methods, and technology used to gather data (see Chapter 11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step Two: Planning and programming (10-step strategic planning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Build strategic planning using a detailed 10-step strategic planning outline that clarifies the difference between strategy and tactics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps include how to identify publics, how to write objectives for each target public, and how to apply working theory to developing program strategy; emphasizes rationale for strategic planning and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify target publics
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and segment target publics as a core part of planning and programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target publics are identified as a discrete step within the 10-step planning outline; objectives are written for each target public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write program objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Write clear objectives for each target public as part of program planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives tie to goals and publics; used to measure program success and guide strategies and tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy vs. tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate strategy (the rationale and overall approach) from tactics (the specific actions and tools used).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 12 emphasizes applying theory to strategy development and reserving tactics for implementation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step Three: Taking action and communicating
rubrics_metrics.description: Design and implement action and communication programs—taking action (including corrective action) in addition to communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers The Action Program and The Communication Program, message crafting/framing/encoding/decoding, message delivery, diffusion processes, and the role of opinion leaders; includes barriers to implementation and crisis communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message development (crafting, framing, encoding/decoding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft, frame, encode and decode messages to achieve effective communication grounded in theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New sections offer concrete, theory-grounded tips for message development; examples illustrate framing and dissemination strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diffusion and opinion leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider diffusion processes and the role of opinion leaders when planning message spread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 13 discusses how information diffuses and how opinion leaders influence adoption and public response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step Four: Evaluating the program
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan and conduct program evaluation to track progress and assess impact across three phases: preparation, implementation, and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expanded sections on measurement, evaluation and metrics include evaluation research process and steps, levels of program evaluation, interpreting and using results, and examples of models and practical methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation research methods (content analysis, surveys)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use content analysis for tracking program implementation and survey research to measure program impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 14 provides practical methods for evaluation research and guidance on interpreting results; stresses the push for measurable results and preparing for evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalism and ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand the professional and ethical principles that underpin public relations practice, including criteria of a profession, ethical foundations, and codes of ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 5 covers professional associations, specialized educational preparation, the body of research and knowledge, codes of ethics, and accountability issues such as licensing and accreditation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal considerations relevant to PR practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand legal issues vital to PR practice: First Amendment, free press and media relations, government access and public affairs, corporate expression, lobbying, employee and labor relations, investor relations, protecting PR materials, reputation/defamation/privacy, and litigation public relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 6 explicitly connects legal topics to specific PR concerns and provides examples of how law impacts practice in the U.S. and other countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical underpinnings: systems perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply systems theory as a theoretical foundation—distinguishing open systems (adaptive) from closed systems (reactive) and using an open systems model for public relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 7 outlines ecological and systems approaches, goal states, structure, cybernetics in open systems, and presents an open systems model of PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication theories and public opinion contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ communication and public opinion theories: dissemination vs communication, mass communication model elements, mass communication effects, public opinion dimensions, orientation and coorientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 8 frames communication theory within the systems perspective and links theory to PR practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal relations and employee communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Design internal communication programs considering organizational culture, regulatory and business contexts, and goals of employee communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 9 discusses importance of internal relations, cultural contexts, regulatory considerations, and both traditional and new media for internal publics.

rubrics_metrics.name: External media and media relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage relations with traditional and new media, understanding new uses of old media and challenges/opportunities of blogs, email, social media and other new media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 10 covers new media's effect on organization–public interactions and practical guidance on working with the media to build and maintain media relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research methods and listening as systematic research
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a research attitude and use both informal (exploratory) and formal research methods, including listening as a systematic research approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 11 emphasizes the role of research in strategic planning, outlines methods and technologies for data gathering, and distinguishes exploratory from formal methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program implementation planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for program implementation as an explicit step in the public relations plan, anticipating barriers and implementation needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 12 and 13 include planning for implementation, barriers to implementation, and the need for corrective actions during execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context-specific practice considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapt PR practice to specific organizational contexts (business and industry; government and politics; military public affairs; nonprofits and NGOs; health care; education; associations and unions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapters 15–21 present unique goals, challenges, legal/regulatory/privacy issues, professionalism, social media and globalization impacts, stakeholder expectations, and examples relevant to each sector (e.g., corporate social responsibility, informing constituents, transparency in military affairs, protecting patient privacy in health care, funding/accountability in education, mobilizing support in unions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement, evaluation, and metrics (expanded focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ measurable metrics and evaluation frameworks to demonstrate program results and accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preface notes expanded sections on measurement and metrics; Chapter 14 details levels of evaluation and how to interpret and use results for accountability and program improvement.
